The Secoya, who call themselves Siekopa'ai or Aido Pãi, are an Indigenous people of the upper Amazon, living along the Aguarico, Santa María and Putumayo rivers on the border of Ecuador and Peru. They speak a Western Tucanoan language, close to that of the Siona.

Jesuit missionaries reached them in the 1600s, and the rubber boom brought epidemics and forced labour. From the 1960s oil drilling in the Ecuadorian Amazon polluted their rivers, and the Secoya joined other peoples in the long lawsuits against the oil companies. Their neighbours include the Napo Kichwa. Their language belongs to the Tucanoan family.
